title: Adaptive midpoint bound for average length
statement: Let $m$ be a nonnegative integer, let $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be nonnegative on $[0,1]$, and suppose that whenever $a+b,a-b\in[0,1]$, $P(a)\le\frac12\bigl(\sqrt{P(a+b)^2+b^2}+\sqrt{P(a-b)^2+b^2}\bigr)$. For real $a,b,t,c$ with $a+b,a-b\in[0,1]$, $t\in[0,1]$, and $c\ge0$, and vectors $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, the symmetric average length at $(t,c)$ is at most the average of its values at $(1,c+((1-t)b)^2)$ and $(2t-1,c+((1-t)b)^2)$.
hypotheses_covered: P is a real-valued profile nonnegative on [0,1]
P satisfies the stated two-point inequality whenever a+b and a-b lie in [0,1]
replaced: For a profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $a,b,t,c\in\mathbb R$, and $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, define $L(t,c)=\frac12\bigl(\sqrt{P(a+tb)^2+c+\|u+tv\|_2^2}+\sqrt{P(a-tb)^2+c+\|u-tv\|_2^2}\bigr)$. Assume $P\ge0$ on $[0,1]$ and, whenever $z\pm d\in[0,1]$, $P(z)\le\bigl(\sqrt{P(z+d)^2+d^2}+\sqrt{P(z-d)^2+d^2}\bigr)/2$. If $a\pm b\in[0,1]$, $0\le t\le1$, and $c\ge0$, then $L(t,c)\le\bigl(L(1,c+((1-t)b)^2)+L(2t-1,c+((1-t)b)^2)\bigr)/2$.
